title: Velocity-Forecast Sampling for Flow-Matching Heads: A Negative Result

contributions.purpose: Speed up inference of flow-matching heads in autoregressive image generation.
contributions.mechanism: Velocity-Forecast Sampling (VFS), a training-free method that speculatively reuses velocity predictions across ODE steps, verifying via MSE-based drift detection and falling back to standard sampling on rejection.
contributions.evaluation: On NextStep-1.1 with GenEval, VFS reaches competitive speedup (1.18-1.76x) but GenEval quality only 0.527-0.567.
contributions.domain: Inference acceleration for flow-matching heads in autoregressive image generation.
contributions.source_quote: We propose Velocity-Forecast Sampling (VFS), a training-free speculative method for accelerating flow-matching heads in autoregressive image generation.

contributions.purpose: Report that the proposed method does not help.
contributions.mechanism: Systematic evaluation comparing VFS against simple ODE step reduction on the quality-speed Pareto frontier.
contributions.evaluation: VFS is Pareto-dominated: the 10-step ODE baseline gives higher quality (GenEval 0.580 vs 0.527-0.567) and competitive speedup (1.68x vs 1.18-1.76x); a negative result.
contributions.domain: Inference acceleration for flow-matching heads in autoregressive image generation.
contributions.source_quote: We provide systematic experimental evidence that VFS is Pareto-dominated by simple step reduction, establishing a negative result for speculative velocity reuse under CFG.

contributions.purpose: Explain why speculative velocity reuse fails.
contributions.mechanism: Analysis of two limiting factors: classifier-free guidance (CFG) disrupts velocity-field smoothness, and the FM head is a small share of latency.
contributions.evaluation: CFG yields only 12-21% per-step acceptance; FM head is ~31% of per-token latency, capping FM-head-only speedup at ~1.45x.
contributions.domain: Inference acceleration for flow-matching heads in autoregressive image generation.
contributions.source_quote: We analyze why speculative approaches fail for CFG-guided flow-matching heads, providing actionable insights for future efficiency research in autoregressive image generation.

self_declared_provenance.quote: VFS is inspired by recent work on speculative flow matching (Bajpai et al., 2026), but specifically targets the per-token flow-matching heads in autoregressive image generation under classifier-free guidance (CFG).

FlowCast (Bajpai et al., 2026) is most closely related to our work, proposing trajectory forecasting for speculative flow matching in diffusion models. However, FlowCast operates on unconditional or text-conditioned diffusion without classifier-free guidance (CFG), whereas our work specifically investigates CFG-guided flow-matching heads in autoregressive image generation, where we find that CFG fundamentally disrupts the velocity smoothness that speculative methods rely upon.

notes: Explicit negative result (stated in the title and abstract): VFS is Pareto-dominated by simple step reduction; reducing steps from 28 to 10 actually improves quality, suggesting the default configuration is over-stepped.
